title: Access Graph & RoleMap: RBAC v2 resource hierarchy and permissions matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Produce the canonical role model (RoleMap) and resource hierarchy for RBAC v2 that supports multi-tenant isolation (hosted/dedicated/private), fine-grained scopes, and an auditable permissions matrix. Deliverables: 1) resource hierarchy diagram and canonical resource identifiers; 2) roles, scopes, and permission matrix CSV; 3) compatibility mapping for SSO/SAML groups, SCIM sync, and console admin controls; 4) audit-event spec for permission checks and admin actions. Scope: design only — implementation tickets will be split into runtime enforcement, policy store, console UI, and audit pipeline. Out of scope for this ticket: migration automation scripts (future ticket).
activity: 2025-02-14 - Ticket created: initial problem framing and success criteria. Noted need to support both tenant-level and resource-level delegation (e.g., project:read vs dataset:read).

2025-02-15 - Architecture sync with Runtime team (Attendees: Marcus, Priya, Omar). Decision: represent resources as hierarchical canonical IDs (org:project:resource_type:resource_id) to allow efficient prefix-based checks and cache-friendly KV lookups.

2025-02-17 - Early trade-off: considered attribute-based access control (ABAC) vs hierarchical RBAC. Chose hybrid approach: primary model RBAC with scope expressions (resource prefixes + predicates) to avoid complexity of full ABAC for first rollout.
2025-02-19 - PM review (Eleni): requested clearer mapping for enterprise SSO flows and service principals. Action: add SCIM and SAML group-to-role mapping examples in matrix.

2025-02-20 - Design review (Tom, Design): UX constraints: admin console must surface effective permissions and inheritance; proposed 'effective role inspector' UI pattern. Follow-up: link to mockups in Confluence (see attachments).

2025-02-22 - Security review kickoff: baseline controls documented. Requirement: all admin role assignments must generate high-fidelity audit events with before/after state and actor identity (SAML Assertion ID when available).

2025-02-24 - Draft permission matrix completed (attached). Includes: primitive actions (read, write, manage, grant), composite roles (Viewer, Editor, Billing Admin, Org Admin), and resource-scoped roles (Project Viewer, DedicatedCluster Operator).

2025-02-25 - Engineering feedback: runtime enforcement must support fast allow/deny short-circuit path for common token checks (api:generate), and a slower evaluation path for cross-tenant policy lookups. Added requirement for TTL-ed role cache invalidation hook when role bindings change.

2025-02-26 - Blocker identified: current audit pipeline only persists event IDs and not the full pre/post state for role assignment changes. Created follow-up ticket ENG-8627 to extend audit event schema and storage retention for admin mutations.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical resource id scheme defined (examples for org, project, model, deployment, dedicated-cluster)
Permission primitives and composite roles enumerated in a CSV-compatible matrix
SAML/SCIM group mapping examples included and described for SCIM sync edge cases
Audit-event spec includes fields: actor_id, actor_provider, action, resource_id, before_bindings, after_bindings, assertion_id (optional), timestamp
Design doc reviewed by Runtime, Console, and Security owners and no major unresolved blockers
notes: Resource hierarchy example: org:acme -> project:acme/infra -> model:acme/infra/bert-quant -> deployment:bert-quant-prod
Scope expression language: allow prefixes with optional qualifiers (e.g., project:acme/*:read, model:*/:annotate[user-owned])
Migration plan: soft-enforce mode for 6 weeks where old RBAC v1 entries are mirrored into RoleMap with 'legacy' tag — separate ticket will cover tooling
Performance target: authorization check P95 <= 1.5ms on cached path; cold evaluation path P95 <= 12ms
Open question: how to represent cross-tenant delegated roles for partner integrations — proposed pattern: external_principal:{provider}:{id} mapped to transient role bindings
